sericulture.content:
In sericulture, ozone is considered an alternative for part of thermal and chemical operations during cocoon preparation and textile post-processing. The main value is cold disinfection and oxidation of odor-forming compounds without adding excess moisture.

For factories, this means cleaner storage chambers, lower biological risk, and better retention of silk thread parameters for subsequent reeling.
benefits: Lower bioload on cocoon surfaces and in storage chambers
Reduction of ammonia and volatile organic odors
Lower water and chemical use in selected preparation steps
More stable lot quality before reeling
Safer working conditions with sealed systems
Straightforward integration into HACCP and internal quality SOPs

intro.paragraph1: Sericulture performance depends on two factors: sanitary stability of raw cocoons and preservation of fiber structure. In conventional thermal stifling, some plants face high energy costs, odors, and uneven lot quality.
intro.paragraph2: Ozone technology works as a controlled cold treatment: gas is supplied to a sealed chamber with a defined concentration and exposure time, followed by ventilation and residual ozone control.

protocol.title: Technology framework:
protocol.text: In practice, concentration and exposure ranges are selected for cocoon type, bed thickness, temperature, and humidity. Operating parameters should always be confirmed by pilot tests at each site.

advantages.title: Why factories consider ozone in sericulture
items: Cold disinfection without boiling and without over-wetting raw material
Lower mold and secondary contamination risk during storage
Deodorization of process zones and warehouses
Integration with ventilation, ORP monitoring, and safety automation
Stepwise deployment model: pilot -> line -> scale-up

geography.title: Major sericulture countries and ozone deployment potential
geography.intro: ISC statistics show that the core of the industry is concentrated in Asia. This is where ozone often has the highest economic impact due to cocoon processing scale and export quality requirements.
tableData: Biological risk reduction and stable quality at industrial scale

steps.title: Line audit
steps.description: Assess losses, energy profile, odor load, microbiology, and quality bottlenecks in current cocoon handling.

steps.title: Pilot chamber
steps.description: Install a sealed pilot chamber with concentration, temperature, humidity, and exposure-time control.

steps.title: Regime tuning
steps.description: Tune operating windows for cocoon variety and tray-bed thickness.

steps.title: Safety layer
steps.description: Deploy ventilation, leak sensors, interlocks, and operator access protocols.

steps.title: Quality KPIs
steps.description: Track thread strength, color, residual moisture, microbiology, and reject rate by lot.

steps.title: Scale-up
steps.description: After KPI confirmation, expand to production capacity and lock into SOP.

items.title: Raw material hygiene
items.description: Reduced microbial load without aggressive chemistry and without water saturation of cocoons.

items.title: Color and structure stability
items.description: Less thermal stress on fiber when operating windows are tuned correctly.

items.title: Lower odor burden
items.description: Ozone oxidizes compounds responsible for strong process-zone odors.

items.title: Lower operating expenses
items.description: Reduced share of heating costs and part of sanitation chemicals.

items.title: Environmental compliance
items.description: Fits well into green textile strategies and export market requirements.

items.title: Scalable deployment
items.description: Can start with a pilot and scale to full capacity without stopping the whole plant.
